input: A defect-reduction project has been carried out on a moulding cell with the aim of reducing the level of rejects produced by the cell, and the results obtained over the course of one quarter are summarised here. Over the quarter in question, the reject rate was cut from 5.4% to 2.8%, which corresponds to a reduction of 2.6 percentage points. When this improvement is considered in the context of the cell's annual production volume of 312k units per year, the change avoids about 8112 rejected units per year, representing a substantial improvement in the overall performance of the cell. It should, however, be borne in mind that the quarter in question included a planned shutdown, and the rates that are reported here are not adjusted for it, which means that the shutdown period forms part of the basis on which the rates have been calculated. Nevertheless, the reduction that has been achieved is considerable, and the project demonstrates the value of a systematic approach to defect reduction in terms of the number of units that are no longer produced as rejects. Going forward, it will be important to monitor the reject rate on an ongoing basis in order to ensure that the improvement that has been achieved is sustained over time and that the annualised benefit continues to be realised in practice across the full production year.
target: A defect-reduction project on a moulding cell cut the reject rate from 5.4% to 2.8% over one quarter, a reduction of 2.6 percentage points. The reject rate is rejected units over units produced in the same period, and both rates are the recorded rates for the cell. At 312k units per year, the change avoids about 8112 rejected units per year. The avoided-units figure applies the rate reduction from one quarter to a full year at the stated volume, so it is an annualised figure built from one quarter's rates, and it holds only while the volume and the reduced rate both hold. The quarter included a planned shutdown, and the rates are not adjusted for it. The shutdown sits inside the production base on which the rates were computed, and production lost to the shutdown is not separated from production lost to rejects. A reader comparing this quarter with a quarter that ran without a shutdown should treat the rate comparison as a comparison of recorded rates, not of rates on a like-for-like running time. The result the project claims is the rate reduction itself, measured on the cell over the quarter. The annual figure states what that reduction is worth in units at the cell's present volume; it is not a separate measurement, and it moves with the volume if the volume changes. The two figures together give the finding and its scale: the rate fell by more than half on the recorded basis, and at the present annual volume the fall corresponds to the stated number of units that no longer come off the cell as rejects.
